candidates.name: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
support_spans: he had hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion
contradict_spans: Initial CSF studies were negative for acid-fast bacilli, herpes simplex virus PCR, and fungi
Rickettsial studies, multiple viral cultures including John Cunningham virus PCR... were also negative
candidates.why: The patient's immunocompromised state due to hepatitis C and heroin use, along with the presence of white matter lesions on MRI, raises suspicion for PML, despite initial negative JC virus PCR.
candidates.protected_reason: PML is a rare and often missed diagnosis, particularly in patients without a clear history of immunosuppression, and requires a high index of suspicion to diagnose.

candidates.name: Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis with Septic Emboli
support_spans: febrile and intermittently responsive
leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
contradict_spans: Transthoracic echocardiography showed no valvular vegetations
candidates.why: The patient's fever, leukocytosis, and history of intravenous drug use raise concern for endocarditis, even in the absence of visible vegetations on echocardiography, as the diagnosis can be challenging.
candidates.protected_reason: Subacute bacterial endocarditis can be difficult to diagnose, especially in the early stages or without obvious valvular disease, making it a consideration in febrile patients with neurological deficits.

candidates.name: CNS Vasculitis
support_spans: Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect
Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema
contradict_spans: Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
candidates.why: The presence of focal neurological deficits and imaging findings suggestive of ischemia or inflammation in the basal ganglia, along with CSF pleocytosis, could indicate CNS vasculitis.
candidates.protected_reason: CNS vasculitis is a rare condition that can present with a wide range of neurological symptoms and imaging findings, making it easily missed without a high index of suspicion.
